---
title: "Running Scenarios"
---

A district has a fixed budget, a measured prevalence, a known resistance level, and a
shortlist of net products. It has to work out which campaign, run against that same
baseline, produces the fewest clinical cases. That means building several scenarios
that differ only in the campaign, running them together, and comparing the results.

`run_scenarios` does all of that in one call. It derives `dn0` from the net mix and the
resistance level, inverts the measured prevalence to an EIR, assembles the twelve
static covariates, and runs the emulator over the 157-window grid. What comes back is one
row per scenario. Scalar summaries and full trajectories sit side by side.

The function is exported from `estimint` but drives both packages. The inversion uses
estiMINT's XGBoost models, while the trajectories come from stateMINT's Mamba2
emulator.

::: {.chapter-outline}
- [One call, end to end](run-scenarios.qmd) — the `Scenario` and `EirTarget` fields, and every column that comes back.
- [A scenario grid](scenario-grid.qmd) — five candidate campaigns against one baseline.
- [Comparing campaigns](comparing.qmd) — rankings, trajectories, and cases averted.
- [Exporting results](exporting.qmd) — scalar summaries to CSV, trajectories to a tidy table R can read.
:::

The worked example throughout is one district with under-5 prevalence 0.45, pyrethroid
resistance 0.30, pyrethroid-only nets at 0.70 coverage, `Q0 = 0.85`,
`phi_bednets = 0.80`, perennial transmission, and neither IRS nor LSM in place.
